title: The Midnight Reservation
venue: The Velvet Cypress Supper Club • Fictional Baton Rouge, Louisiana
description: A silent investor is killed near the black-curtain corridor while the music continues. This hard case uses sound, movement tags, scent, fibers, and hidden reservation ledgers to test a sophisticated alibi.

answerKey.method: Used a brass curtain tieback in the black-curtain corridor and covered the attack with a prerecorded audio segment.
answerKey.motive: To protect an off-book midnight reservation cash scheme that Nathalie was about to shut down.
answerKey.keyEvidence: Audio automation log, empty booth reflection, staff tag movement, violet perfume and fiber trace, and hidden-table ledger.
answerKey.explanation: Cressida’s live-DJ alibi was false because the music was automated. Her tag left the booth, trace evidence tied her to the corridor, and the booking ledger gave her a motive to stop Nathalie.

publicClues.title: Case Opened
publicClues.text: Silent investor Nathalie Quinn is found in the black-curtain corridor after a midnight private reservation. The dining room’s sound system kept playing as if no one left the room.

publicClues.title: Live Scene Update
publicClues.text: The entertainment director says the DJ booth never went unattended. Then the audio screen shows a preloaded set running without a live operator.

publicClues.title: Detective Decision 1 Available
publicClues.text: The first decision depends on whether the corridor death was hidden by sound and timing.

publicClues.title: Live Scene Update
publicClues.text: A curtain hook clinks when security opens the corridor. Cressida Ward flinches before anyone says what was found there.

publicClues.title: Detective Decision 2 Available
publicClues.text: The first timeline gap now involves a prerecorded sound cue and a missing booth operator.

publicClues.title: Live Scene Update
publicClues.text: The reservation screen flickers. One canceled “midnight table” reappears for half a second under a false initials-only booking.

publicClues.title: Detective Decision 3 Available
publicClues.text: Forensic findings can now separate a fall from staged corridor contact.

publicClues.title: Live Scene Update
publicClues.text: A witness says the corridor smelled like expensive violet perfume, not kitchen smoke. Cressida’s scarf carries the same scent, but so do the curtain ropes.

publicClues.title: Detective Decision 4 Available
publicClues.text: The motive hides inside private booking kickbacks and a closing investment vote.

publicClues.title: Live Scene Update
publicClues.text: The room is silent when the audio automation log plays back. The applause track fires at 8:48 PM, exactly when someone needed the corridor noise covered.

publicClues.title: Final Accusation Open
publicClues.text: The corridor, automation log, fibers, private booking ledger, and false alibi are ready for final accusation.

phone.title: Nathalie’s Draft Note
phone.text: Nathalie drafted a note at 8:34 PM: “Close the off-book tables tonight. C.W. cannot keep taking cash.”

phone.title: Silent Mode Change
phone.text: Cressida’s phone entered Do Not Disturb at 8:43 PM and reconnected at 8:51 PM.

messages.title: Initials-Only Booking
messages.text: A message to Cressida reads: “Midnight reservation is cash only. No full names.”

messages.title: Threat From Nathalie
messages.text: Nathalie wrote, “If I see another hidden table tonight, I remove you from the entertainment contract.”

maps.title: Booth Location Gap
maps.text: Cressida’s staff tag leaves the DJ booth zone at 8:46 PM, during a preloaded track segment.

maps.title: Corridor Return
maps.text: The same tag returns from the black-curtain corridor at 8:50 PM, just before the live mic comes back.

bank.title: Cash Table Pattern
bank.text: Three private deposits match initials-only reservations handled through entertainment rather than the front desk.

bank.title: Contract Loss
bank.text: If Nathalie closed the hidden-table scheme, Cressida would lose the lounge programming contract and the off-book cash stream.

photos.title: Curtain Tieback Photo
photos.text: A photo from the corridor shows one brass tieback hook missing and a dark fiber caught on the remaining bracket.

photos.title: DJ Booth Reflection
photos.text: A mirrored wall photo shows the booth chair empty while the music display still reads “LIVE SET.”

social.title: Lounge Clip
social.text: A guest clip includes an applause swell at 8:48 PM, but no one in the room is clapping.

social.title: Deleted Promo Post
social.text: Cressida deleted a promo promising “midnight tables for people who know how to ask.”

contacts.title: Witness Statement: Iris Bell
contacts.text: Iris says Nathalie left the investor table after whispering, “I am ending the midnight list.”

contacts.title: Witness Statement: Cressida Ward
contacts.text: Cressida says she was live-mixing in the DJ booth from 8:40 PM to 8:55 PM and never entered the corridor.

contacts.title: Witness Statement: Malik Dorsey
contacts.text: Malik says the music never changed, but he did not actually see Cressida at the controls during the applause swell.

contacts.title: Witness Statement: Vera St. John
contacts.text: Vera says the corridor smelled strongly of violet perfume after the body was found, and Cressida had been wearing that scent all evening.

notes.title: Detective Note: Sound Is Alibi
notes.text: In this case, sound may create a false alibi. A continuous track does not prove a person stayed at the booth.

notes.title: Detective Note: Corridor Physics
notes.text: The bruising pattern and missing brass tieback matter because a simple fall would not remove hardware from the wall.

files.title: Audio Automation Log
files.text: The DJ software shows a 7-minute automation block starting at 8:45 PM.

files.title: Private Booking Ledger
files.text: The initials-only midnight tables were managed under Cressida’s entertainment account, not the normal reservation system.

browser.title: Search Cache
browser.text: Cressida searched “disable live booth presence indicator” before doors opened.

browser.title: Contract Clause
browser.text: The entertainment contract ends immediately if off-book reservations are confirmed.

openingNarration: Welcome to The Midnight Reservation. This is a hard case: trust the timeline you build, not the soundscape the room gives you.
revealScript: The case closes on Cressida Ward. She hid behind music, perfume, and private luxury, but the timeline cut through the performance. The midnight list was motive, the corridor was method, and the prerecorded applause was cover.

seriesArc: Three separate mysteries inside a fictional upscale Baton Rouge supper club inspired by candlelit fine dining, dress-code drama, private tables, and late-night lounge energy.
lobbyBackstory: The Velvet Cypress Supper Club is hosting a private investor dinner behind black curtains and curated sound. When Nathalie Quinn is found in the corridor, the music keeps playing — and that may be the first lie.
rsvpExcerpt: A private investor dies while the music never stops. In this hard mystery, the alibi is hidden inside sound, scent, movement, and a midnight reservation no one was supposed to see.
